request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have a from-date and an optional to-date, and a person can have several of them. All 4 Playwright tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V29__person_hold.sql`, adds a `person_hold` table with one row per hold. The old `held` yes/no column is dropped. Anyone who was held before keeps one hold with no end date that covers all claim dates, so their totals don't change.
- **Server:**
  - The hold endpoint now takes from/to dates. A blank from-date means the sheet's today; a blank to-date means the hold has no end. A bad date, or a to-date before the from-date, is refused and nothing is written.
  - Each hold writes `PERSON_HELD sheet=… by=… name=<name> from=<date>`. Releasing and `PERSON_RELEASED` are gone.
  - One rule now decides whether a claim counts (`Person.counts(Claim)`). An OPEN or PENDING claim is left out only if its date falls within one of the person's holds. A claim bound by a statement always counts.
  - That rule is used everywhere totals are worked out: the rollup audit lines, statements and closing a period.
- **Front end:**
  - The same rule is applied to every total on screen: the person's own totals, the sheet totals, periods, the summary, patrons and the CSV export.
  - The person row shows `person-hold` as yes/no for "has any hold", and lists each hold as a `person-hold-line`.
  - It has `person-hold-from` and `person-hold-to` inputs. The `person-hold-toggle` button is kept but now only adds a hold.

**Choices worth checking**
- Both the from-date and the to-date count as inside the hold.
- A PENDING claim never counts as bound by a statement for this rule. This matches how the app already shows PENDING claims at their live figure rather than the statement's figure.
- Holds can't be edited or deleted, because the request only says a hold ends on its to-date.
